Mondstadt: The City of Freedom.heading: The Cradle of Freedom in the North
paragraphs: Situated in the northeast of the continent of Teyvat, Mondstadt is the realm of the Anemo Archon Barbatos and the historical birthplace of the philosophy of mortal liberty. Surrounded by Cider Lake and protected by limestone battlements and turning windmills, the city of Mondstadt stands as an open sanctuary where artists, bards, vintners, and travelers mingle freely without aristocratic decrees or religious mandates.

Mondstadt's geography is remarkably diverse: from the fertile vineyards of Dawn Winery and the peaceful springs of Springvale to the howling winds of Stormbearer Point, the ancient ruins of Stormterror's Lair, and the looming, snow-swept frozen peaks of Dragonspine in the south. The land is cooled by perpetual breezes that carry the sweet scent of Dandelion seeds and Cecilias across the grassy hills.

Mondstadt: The City of Freedom.heading: Historical Foundations: Rebellion Against Two Tyrannies
paragraphs: Mondstadt's culture of freedom was forged through two bloody revolutions. The first occurred 2,600 years ago when the poet-bard and the wind sprite Barbatos overthrew Decarabian, the God of Storms, shattering the frozen storm walls of Old Mondstadt. The second revolution occurred 1,000 years ago, after the noble Lawrence Clan corrupted the nation into an aristocratic slave state; the gladiator slave Vennessa, aided by the returned Barbatos and the dragon Dvalin, overthrew the tyrants and established the Knights of Favonius.

Because its liberty was twice bought with blood, the people of Mondstadt fiercely resist any centralization of authoritarian power. While the Knights of Favonius handle municipal defense and the Church of Favonius preserves spiritual rituals, neither body claims sovereign royal ownership over the citizens.

Mondstadt: The City of Freedom.heading: The Four Winds and Elemental Protectors
paragraphs: To ensure Mondstadt would remain safe while he wandered the world in freedom, Barbatos appointed the Four Winds to watch over the realm: the Dragon of the East (Dvalin), the Wolf of the North (Andrius / Lupus Boreas), the Lion of the South (the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, inherited from Vennessa), and the Falcon of the West (Vennessa herself following her celestial ascension).

Even when mortal memory fades or dragons fall into corrupted slumber, these ancient spiritual guardians remain anchored to Mondstadt's soil. In moments of dire peril—such as the Cataclysm five hundred years ago when the abyssal shadow dragon Durin invaded—the winds united to defend the city and cast the monster down into the frozen wastes of Dragonspine.

Mondstadt: The City of Freedom.heading: Mysteries on the Northern Frontier
paragraphs: While often viewed by foreign diplomats as peaceful, sleepy, and drunk on Dandelion Wine, Mondstadt harbors some of the most dangerous metaphysical secrets in Teyvat. Beneath the Cathedral sits the forbidden vault holding ancient relics; within the mountains sits Albedo, the homunculus created by the outlaw alchemist Rhinedottir; and to the north lies the mysterious gateway toward Nod-Krai and the Dark Sea where Grand Master Varka leads Mondstadt's elite expedition.

As the first nation to welcome the Traveler, Mondstadt represents both the start of the journey and an enduring emotional home. Its people live by the joyful wisdom of their unseen god: 'Fly, fly away; like a bird in the sky, bear the world's sorrows with song.'

Liyue: A Harbor of Contracts.heading: The Ancient Jewel of the East
paragraphs: Perched along the southern coast of the continent, Liyue Harbor is the oldest continuously inhabited mortal city in Teyvat, boasting over 3,700 years of unbroken history. Blessed with deep natural harbors, rich mineral veins, and mountain valleys guarded by the Adepti, Liyue is the heart of continental commerce, maritime shipping, and artisan craftsmanship.

Everything in Liyue operates on the sacred principle of the 'Contract'—a cultural bedrock established by Morax (Rex Lapis), the God of Contracts and Geo Archon. To the people of Liyue, a signed contract is not merely legal paper; it is a spiritual vow that binds buyer and seller, ruler and citizen, god and mortal. Breaking a contract is considered the highest sacrilege, inviting the wrath of the rock.

Liyue: A Harbor of Contracts.heading: The Adepti and the Pact of Mt. Tianheng
paragraphs: Liyue's survival through the bloody Archon War was guaranteed by Morax and the illuminated Adepti of Jueyun Karst—celestial beasts and immortal spirits such as Cloud Retainer, Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver, Streetward Rambler (Madame Ping), and the Yakshas. Thousands of years ago, Morax and the Adepti signed an eternal pact to protect Liyue Harbor from the wrath of ancient gods, sea monsters, and demons.

While mortals lived in the bustling docks below, the Adepti resided in solitude among the floating mist islands and soaring amber karst pillars of Jueyun Karst, stepping forward only when existential disasters threatened the realm. Among them, the Conqueror of Demons, Xiao, continues to fight alone in the shadows, bearing the agonizing weight of karmic debt to purge lingering demonic remnants from the earth.

Liyue: A Harbor of Contracts.heading: From the Rule of Gods to the Age of Humanity
paragraphs: For nearly four millennia, Rex Lapis personally descended every year during the Rite of Descension to deliver prophecies that set the financial and agricultural course of the nation. However, following the orchestrated 'death' of Rex Lapis during the Rite of Descension and the climactic defeat of the ancient sea god Osial by the united forces of the Liyue Qixing, the Millelith, and the Adepti, Liyue underwent a historic metamorphosis.

Recognizing that humanity had matured enough to shoulder their own burdens, the Adepti formally ceded administrative and political authority to the mortal council of the Liyue Qixing under Ningguang and Keqing. The Golden House ceased to mint new Mora through divine power, marking the triumphant end of the divine contract and the dawn of an era where mortal trade, law, and perseverance shape the nation's future.

Liyue: A Harbor of Contracts.heading: Geographical Splendor and Hidden Depths
paragraphs: Beyond the grand red pavilions of the harbor, Liyue stretches across breathtaking landscapes: the mist-shrouded tea terraces of Chenyu Vale, the terraced water fields of Qingce Village, the rocky labyrinth of Guyun Stone Forest, and the terrifying, abyssal chasm known simply as The Chasm. Within The Chasm's underground mines, ancient celestial nails, Khaenri'ahn ruins, and dark abyssal oozes reveal that Liyue's mountains conceal secrets as deep and ancient as the world itself.

Inazuma: Islands and Eternity.heading: The Thunder-Swept Archipelago
paragraphs: Isolated far across the eastern sea, Inazuma is an archipelago of six distinct, tempest-tossed volcanic islands governed by the Electro Archon, the Raiden Shogun. Characterized by purple lightning, cherry blossom groves, crashing waves, and traditional Japanese-inspired aesthetics, Inazuma stands as an ancient realm deeply steeped in martial honor, spiritual purification, and the divine pursuit of 'Eternity.'

Each island of the archipelago possesses its own unique ecosystem and dark history: Narukami Island hosts the grand Tenshukaku palace, Inazuma City, and Mt. Yougou's Sacred Sakura; Kannazuka houses the colossal Tatarasuna smelting forge; Yashiori Island is cleaved in half by the colossal skeleton of the slain serpent god Orobashi; Watatsumi Island flourishes with coral reefs and moonlight shrines; Seirai Island crackles with eternal storms; and Tsurumi Island sleeps under a cursed, ghost-haunted sea fog.

Inazuma: Islands and Eternity.heading: The Tri-Commission and Feudal Governance
paragraphs: The civil governance of Inazuma is divided among three great hereditary bureaucratic houses known collectively as the Tri-Commission, reporting directly to the Raiden Shogun: the Yashiro Commission (the Kamisato Clan, overseeing religious ceremonies, shrines, festivals, and cultural heritage), the Tenryou Commission (the Kujou Clan, commanding the shogunate army, police, and homeland defense), and the Kanjou Commission (the Hiiragi Clan, managing maritime customs, foreign trade, and border enforcement).

Working alongside them is the Grand Narukami Shrine, presided over by Guuji Yae Miko—the chief priestess, head of the Yae Publishing House, and an ancient, mischievous Kitsune who has served as Ei's closest confidante for hundreds of years. The shrine oversees the purification of the Ley Lines and the health of the Sacred Sakura, which absorbs the accumulated filth and malice of Inazuma's soil.

Inazuma: Islands and Eternity.heading: The Tragedy of the Decrees and the Civil War
paragraphs: In modern history, Inazuma fell into dark turmoil when the puppet Shogun, manipulated by corrupt commissioners and Fatui agents, instituted the Sakoku Decree (complete border closure to all foreign travel) and the Vision Hunt Decree (the systematic confiscation and stripping of mortal elemental Visions). Deprived of their Visions, many martial artists and citizens lost their memories, passions, and will to live.

In response, the people of Watatsumi Island—who preserve their own ancestral culture under the Divine Priestess Sangonomiya Kokomi—launched a fierce armed resistance against the Shogunate army. The resulting civil war tore families apart until the Traveler, with the support of the resistance, the Kamisato siblings (Ayaka and Ayato), and Yae Miko, challenged the Raiden Shogun in Tenshukaku, confronted Ei within the Plane of Euthymia, and persuaded her to revoke both tyrannical decrees.

Inazuma: Islands and Eternity.heading: A New Dawn for the Realm of Thunder
paragraphs: Following Ei's awakening and her subsequent five-hundred-year duel of will against the puppet Shogun within the realm of Makoto's consciousness, Inazuma has entered a hopeful new era. The borders are reopening to foreign merchants, the commissions have been purged of corruption, and the lingering scars of Orobashi's Tatarigami radiation are being carefully healed.

Inazuma stands today not as an island frozen in fear of celestial destruction, but as a resilient realm where cherry blossoms bloom and fall with grace, embracing the transient beauty of human dreams within the enduring flow of time.

Sumeru: Knowledge and Memory.heading: The Land of Rainforests and Deserts
paragraphs: Encompassing both the most lush, verdant jungles and the most brutally scorching deserts on the continent, Sumeru is the realm of the Dendro Archon and the global capital of scholarship and botanical wisdom. Across the tranquil canopies of the Avidya Forest and Lokapala Jungle, immense divine trees and luminous flora thrive, while to the west, the Great Red Sand stretches into towering sandstone mausoleums, subterranean temples, and howling sandstorms.

Sumeru's foundational culture revolves around the pursuit of knowledge. For thousands of years, the realm was guided by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who created the rainforest from the arid earth, nurtured the childlike forest spirits known as the Aranara, and guarded Irminsul—the colossal subterranean silver tree whose roots connect the memories and elemental circulation of all Teyvat.

Sumeru: Knowledge and Memory.heading: The Ancient Tri-God Alliance of the Desert
paragraphs: Long before the Archon War solidified the modern borders, Sumeru was ruled by a legendary triumvirate of divine friends: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, King Deshret (Al-Ahmar), and the Goddess of Flowers (Nabu Malikata). Together, they created the paradise of Ay-Khanoum ('City of the Moon Maiden'), seeking to cultivate a utopian civilization where mortals could transcend suffering.

However, tragedy struck when the Goddess of Flowers perished, having willingly sacrificed herself to open King Deshret's eyes to the cosmic truths beyond the sky. Consumed by grief and a desperate desire to resurrect her and build a world free from divine tyranny, King Deshret unleashed 'Forbidden Knowledge' from the cosmic void into Teyvat. The alien corruption spawned the deadly disease Eleazar, mutated the desert into chaotic storms, and drove Deshret to madness, forcing him to sacrifice his life while Rukkhadevata expended her divine strength to cleanse the land.

Sumeru: Knowledge and Memory.heading: The Division Between City and Desert
paragraphs: The fall of King Deshret left deep, generational scars across Sumeru. The desert tribes—now wandering as the mercenary Eremites—were marginalized and looked down upon by the arrogant scholars of the Sumeru Akademiya, who hoarded resources in the rainforest and controlled the population through the Akasha Terminal. For centuries, desert dwellers mourned the lost glory of Al-Ahmar, dreaming of a resurrected King Deshret who would topple the Akademiya.

This bitter historical division was finally bridged during the Sumeru Archon Quest, when the Traveler, Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Candace, and Rahman discovered the truth inscribed within King Deshret's mausoleum: that Deshret and Rukkhadevata were never bitter enemies, but devoted allies who fought side-by-side to save the world from abyssal corruption. This revelation dismantled centuries of hatred, paving the way for reconciliation between rainforest and desert.

Sumeru: Knowledge and Memory.heading: The Rebirth of Wisdom Under Lesser Lord Kusanali
paragraphs: Following the rescue of Nahida from the Sanctuary of Surasthana and the heartbreaking, necessary erasure of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from Irminsul's memories, Sumeru is now led by a living god who values empathy and human dreams over cold academic superiority.

With the Akasha Terminal dismantled, scholars and citizens alike are learning to think, imagine, and explore freely once again. Sumeru stands today as a beacon of intellectual light, proving that true wisdom is not found in hoarded data or artificial godhood, but in understanding, compassion, and the interconnected harmony of all living things.

Fontaine: The Nation of Justice.heading: The Elevated Stage of Justice and Drama
paragraphs: Raised high above the rest of Teyvat upon colossal waterfalls and majestic limestone aqueducts, Fontaine is the realm of the Hydro Archon, renowned for its dazzling high culture, haute couture, clockwork robotics (Meka), and legal drama. Centered around the grand Court of Fontaine and the soaring Opera Epiclese, the nation treats judicial trials not merely as sober legal procedures, but as magnificent public spectacles where truth is unveiled like a theatrical climax.

Powered by 'Indemnitium'—a refined elemental energy harvested from the collective faith of the audience during legal trials inside the Opera Epiclese—Fontaine developed the most advanced civilian technology in Teyvat: amphibious transport lines, automated mechanical police, submersibles, and cinema. However, beneath this glamorous facade of justice, the nation lived under the shadow of a terrifying, ancient prophecy.

Fontaine: The Nation of Justice.heading: The Ancient Prophecy and the Sin of Egeria
paragraphs: An ancient stone prophecy carved in the ruins of sunken Remuria foretold Fontaine's total doom: 'The people of Fontaine will dissolve into the water, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping upon her throne.' For centuries, scholars dismissed it as myth, until citizens began tragically dissolving into pure water upon coming into contact with the mysterious Primordial Sea water.

The dark truth of Fontaine's origins traced back to the previous Hydro Archon, Egeria. Longing to grant humanity to her beloved water familiars (the Oceanids), Egeria used the sacred waters of the Primordial Sea to create human bodies, infusing them with Oceanid souls. To Celestia, this act was an unforgivable sacrilege—an illicit usurpation of heaven's divine right to create human life—and the Heavenly Principles decreed that the people would one day be reclaimed by the Primordial Sea.

Fontaine: The Nation of Justice.heading: The Five-Hundred-Year Masquerade
paragraphs: To outwit Celestia and save her people, the subsequent Hydro Archon, Focalors, devised an audacious, agonizing 500-year plan. She split her divine self in two: her divinity remained hidden inside the monumental judicial scale, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, slowly gathering Indemnitium for half a millennium to execute an Archon. Meanwhile, her mortal human body, Furina, was cursed to play the role of an eccentric, arrogant, all-knowing god in public, enduring five centuries of crushing loneliness and terror without ever revealing the secret.

When the Primordial Sea broke through the foundations and the Narwhal from the cosmic abyss assaulted Fontaine, Focalors enacted her final judgment. In the Opera Epiclese, she willingly executed herself, completely destroying the divine Hydro Throne. This permanent destruction returned the complete Hydro Elemental Authority to Neuvillette, the reincarnated Sovereign Dragon of Water.

Fontaine: The Nation of Justice.heading: The Forgiveness of Original Sin and the Reign of the Dragon
paragraphs: With his full dragon authority restored, Neuvillette performed an act of absolute mercy: he used his supreme power over the Primordial Sea to permanently cleanse Fontaine's citizens of their 'original sin,' transforming their Oceanid-infused blood into genuine, true human blood that could never dissolve again.

Though Fontaine was flooded in the climax, not a single human life was lost, fulfilling the wording of the prophecy while defeating its fatal curse. Today, with Furina living in peaceful mortal retirement as an acclaimed stage director, Fontaine is governed by Chief Justice Neuvillette—a just, immortal dragon who judges humanity with deep compassion, standing as a sovereign land free from celestial chains.

Natlan: The Nation of War.heading: The Fiery Bastion of the Sacred Flame
paragraphs: Nestled among towering volcanic canyons, geothermal hot springs, and jagged stone spires in the southwest of Teyvat, Natlan is the realm of the Pyro Archon and the Nation of War. Unlike other nations where peace is maintained through diplomacy or law, Natlan has existed in an unending state of active, heroic warfare for centuries, fighting against the creeping, subterranean corruption of the Abyss that seeks to swallow the world.

Natlan is organized into Six Great Tribes, each residing in a distinct geographical region and sharing an unbreakable bond with a specific breed of Saurian: the Children of the Echoes (Tepetlisaur), the Scions of the Canopy (Yumkasaur), the People of the Springs (Koholasaur), the Flower-Feather Clan (Qucusaur), the Masters of the Night-Wind (Iktomisaur), and the Collective of Plenty (Tatankasaur). Each tribe maintains its own ancestral customs, martial traditions, and heroic totems.

Natlan: The Nation of War.heading: The Ode of Resurrection and the Ancient Names
paragraphs: Central to Natlan's survival is the 'Ode of Resurrection' and the sacred power of 'Ancient Names.' When heroic warriors fall in battle defending the realm from Abyssal incursions, their souls and battle deeds are engraved onto ancestral obsidian tablets within the Night Kingdom—the spiritual realm beneath the physical earth.

Through the sacred flame and the rituals of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, warriors chosen by the sacred flame can be resurrected from the Night Kingdom, returning to their families and tribes to fight another day. However, this resurrection is not guaranteed: if a warrior falls inside deep Abyssal domains where the sacred flame cannot reach, or if their Ancient Name is tainted, their spirit may be permanently lost to the dark.

Natlan: The Nation of War.heading: The Saurians: Dragons Reborn as Kin
paragraphs: In Natlan, dragons are not monstrous enemies to be slain; they are family. Following the defeat of the ancient Dragon Sovereigns millennia ago, the dragons of Natlan gradually evolved into Saurians, shrinking in size and adapting to live in close symbiosis with human tribes. Warriors raise Saurians from hatching, communicating through shared emotions and utilizing their unique abilities to burrow through stone, swing across mountain chasms, or surf upon liquid lava.

Through the mystical art of 'Indwelling,' human warriors can even merge their spiritual consciousness with Saurians, experiencing the world through their heightened primal senses. This intimate cross-species bond makes Natlan unique across all Teyvat: a land where the descendants of the ancient dragon world and the children of humanity stand side-by-side as sworn brethren.

Natlan: The Nation of War.heading: Archon Mavuika and the Final Defense
paragraphs: Natlan's current Pyro Archon is Mavuika, a mortal human warrior from five hundred years ago who was chosen by the sacred flame during the Cataclysm. Foreseeing that the Abyss would launch its ultimate assault five centuries later, Mavuika made the staggering sacrifice of giving up her mortal life, sealing her soul in the sacred flame to reincarnate in the present era when her people would need her most.

Supported by heroic champions like Kachina, Kinich, and Mualani, Mavuika leads Natlan in a desperate, epic struggle against the Abyss. In Natlan, 'War' is not an act of greedy conquest, but a sacred, joyous celebration of life, courage, and camaraderie—a roaring flame that refuses to be extinguished by the dark.

Snezhnaya: A Nation Still Unfolding.heading: The Frozen Citadel of the North
paragraphs: Occupying the freezing northernmost reaches of Teyvat, Snezhnaya is the realm of the Cryo Archon, the Tsaritsa, and the homeland of the formidable Fatui. Shrouded in perpetual blizzards, subzero tundra, and frozen seas, Snezhnaya is widely acknowledged as the most technologically advanced, industrially powerful, and militarily terrifying nation on the continent.

Operating from the soaring, ice-sheathed halls of Zapolyarny Palace, the Tsaritsa commands a sprawling state machinery that blends cutting-edge mechanical engineering, advanced metallurgy, Delusion synthesis, and continental banking networks. To foreigners, Snezhnaya presents a grim, menacing face of cold efficiency, aggressive diplomacy, and ruthless espionage.

Snezhnaya: A Nation Still Unfolding.heading: The Tsaritsa: The God Who Has No Love Left
paragraphs: According to ancient records, the Cryo Archon was once the gentlest deity among the Seven—the God of Love who cherished mortal dreams and wept for the fallen. However, during the Cataclysm five hundred years ago, something horrific occurred in Khaenri'ah that completely hardened her heart. She witnessed divine atrocities that shattered her faith in the Heavenly Principles.

From that day forward, the Tsaritsa cut off all gentle communication with the other Archons and declared war on the heavens. In the words of Dainsleif: 'She is a god with no love left for her people, nor do they have any left for her. Her followers hope only to be on her side when the day of her rebellion against the divine finally arrives.' Her followers do not serve out of blind adoration, but out of grim loyalty to her revolutionary purpose.

Snezhnaya: A Nation Still Unfolding.heading: Culture, Hardship, and the Warmth of Winter
paragraphs: Despite Snezhnaya's fearsome international reputation, its domestic life holds surprising warmth and familial devotion. Surviving in a land where temperatures can freeze a breath into ice requires fierce solidarity among neighbors. Families gather around blazing hearths, sharing hearty stews, fire-water, and folk tales of brave hunters and ice fishers.

The complexity of Snezhnayan culture is epitomized by figures like Tartaglia (Childe), who is simultaneously a bloodthirsty, lethal warrior on the battlefield and an affectionate, protective older brother who spoils his younger siblings with toys from abroad. The people of Snezhnaya endure the harsh ice with pride, viewing their hardships as a crucible that tempers them into unbreakable steel.

Snezhnaya: A Nation Still Unfolding.heading: The Gathering Storm
paragraphs: As the Fatui near the completion of their Gnosis collection, Snezhnaya stands as the inevitable destination where all the threads of Genshin Impact's overarching narrative will converge. Within Zapolyarny Palace, the Jester, the Harbingers, and the Cryo Archon are assembling the final pieces of an apocalyptic offensive.

Whether Snezhnaya's rebellion will liberate Teyvat from the false sky or unleash a catastrophe that consumes the continent remains the paramount question of the entire saga. What is certain is that when the blizzard of Snezhnaya sweeps south, the world will never be the same again.

Nod-Krai: The Northern Borderland.heading: The Frontier Beyond the Horizon
paragraphs: Mentioned in quiet whispers, traveler journals, and official expedition dispatches, Nod-Krai is the remote, mysterious northern borderland region nestled between the frozen frontiers of northern Snezhnaya, the stormy cliffs of Mondstadt's northern coast, and the desolate waters of the Dark Sea. Far removed from the civilized trade routes and well-charted valleys of the Seven Nations, Nod-Krai is an untamed wilderness of pine forests, permafrost plains, and windswept rocky coasts.

Historically, Nod-Krai has served as a buffer zone and migration corridor for hardy frontier clans, exiled scholars, and adventurous trappers. Its geography is shaped by brutal seasonal blizzards and shifting ice sheets that make overland travel perilous for anyone without elite survival experience.

Nod-Krai: The Northern Borderland.heading: Varka's Expedition and Strategic Significance
paragraphs: Nod-Krai gained immense narrative importance in recent lore due to Grand Master Varka's continental expedition. When Varka marched out of Mondstadt with four-fifths of the Knights of Favonius's elite cavalry and veteran knights, their operational route directed them north toward the borderlands of Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya.

It was in this northern frontier that Varka's expedition famously encountered the elite detachment of the Fatui led by Il Capitano (the First Harbinger). Instead of erupting into bloody conflict, the two seasoned commanders shared mutual respect, with Varka sending dispatches back to Mondstadt praising Capitano's chivalry and martial honor. Nod-Krai serves as the staging ground where the superpowers of the north watch one another with measured caution.

Nod-Krai: The Northern Borderland.heading: Ancient Myths of the Frostmoon and the Dark Sea
paragraphs: Beyond contemporary military movements, folklore recorded in ancient texts links Nod-Krai to the enigmatic 'Frostmoon Scions'—ancient tribes that worshipped the lunar cycles long before the Archon War divided the continent. Some legends claim that when the Three Moon Sisters fell from the sky, fragments of celestial moonlight chilled the northern soil, creating zones of perpetual twilight.

Furthermore, because Nod-Krai borders the Dark Sea—the vast oceanic and continental expanse outside the jurisdiction and protection of the Seven Archons—the region occasionally witnesses strange anomalies: ancient gods who fled the Archon War, bizarre mutated beasts, and forgotten ruins that bear neither celestial nor abyssal architecture.

Nod-Krai: The Northern Borderland.heading: An Expanding Chapter of Teyvat's Map
paragraphs: As Teyvat's map continuously expands northward, Nod-Krai stands as one of the most tantalizing frontier regions awaiting full exploration. It represents the meeting point of Snezhnayan iron, Mondstadt chivalry, and primordial northern mythology.

Whether explored through future Archon Quests or expanded world chronicles, Nod-Krai embodies the thrill of true frontier exploration: the edge where the comforting laws of the Archons give way to the wild, untamed unknown.

Teyvat: The Known World.heading: The Continental Tapestry
paragraphs: Teyvat is the known continental world that serves as the stage for Genshin Impact, comprising seven distinct nations ruled by the Seven Archons, alongside forgotten ancient ruins beneath the earth and the mysterious Dark Sea beyond the borders. From the windy plains of Mondstadt and the stone cliffs of Liyue to the islands of Inazuma, the rainforests and deserts of Sumeru, the elevated waters of Fontaine, the volcanic canyons of Natlan, and the frozen tundra of Snezhnaya, Teyvat is a living masterpiece of elemental harmony.

Life across Teyvat is fundamentally driven by the seven elements, which circulate through the continental Ley Line network like blood through veins. Mortals gifted with strong, unyielding ambitions are granted 'Visions' by the heavens, allowing them to channel elemental energy and perform superhuman feats of combat, craftsmanship, and leadership.

Teyvat: The Known World.heading: The Cosmological Structure: The False Sky
paragraphs: While ordinary inhabitants gaze up at the sun, moon, and stars in wonder, the true cosmological architecture of Teyvat is deeply unnatural. During the Unreconciled Stars crisis, the Fatui Harbinger Scaramouche discovered an earth-shattering secret that was later confirmed by Dottore and Pierro: 'The stars, the sky... it's all a gigantic hoax. A lie.'

Teyvat is enclosed within a colossal metaphysical firmament known as the 'False Sky'—a barrier constructed by Celestia and the Primordial One to shield the world from the hostile, alien void outside, while simultaneously keeping humanity locked in an artificial terrarium. Below the earth lies the Abyss, a swirling realm of primordial chaos that constantly seeks to break through the Ley Lines and dissolve the world's structured reality.

Teyvat: The Known World.heading: Cyclic History and Celestial Judgment
paragraphs: Teyvat's history is not linear; it is cyclical. Long before the Seven Archons, the continent was ruled by the Seven Dragon Sovereigns. They were toppled by the Primordial One (the First Descender), who established a unified human civilization. However, whenever human kingdoms advanced too far, uncovered cosmic secrets, or contacted the Abyss, Celestia deployed Celestial Nails to annihilate them, resetting civilization and burying history beneath layers of stone.

Civilizations such as Sal Vindagnyr, Enkanomiya, Gurabad, Remuria, and Khaenri'ah all fell victim to this cyclical cataclysm. The ruins of these fallen realms, littered with inactive Ruin Guards and cryptic stone murals, stand as silent warnings to the surface nations that the peace enforced by the gods comes with a terrifying, conditional price.

Teyvat: The Known World.heading: The Role of Descenders in Shaping Destiny
paragraphs: In this rigidly ordained world where mortal destinies are written into the stars by the Heavenly Principles, only rare entities known as 'Descenders'—beings who originate from outside Teyvat—possess the power to rewrite fate. Because Descenders are not native to this world, their memories and actions cannot be erased or manipulated by Irminsul.

The Traveler, confirmed by Nahida to be the Fourth Descender, represents an unprecedented wildcard in Teyvat's cosmic equation. As the Traveler journeys across the seven nations, witnessing the struggles of mortals and the burdens of gods, they are gradually weaving a new tapestry of destiny—one that may finally shatter the false sky and allow the people of Teyvat to claim their own freedom.
